what: 🫳️ What the five node-graph pointer gestures cost and what they dispatch, over generation3d's own `hexagonal-mushroom-column` flow payload — the same graph `⚙️EngineCanvas/🧫️fixtures/🕸️wgpu-node-graph/🔣️.json` carries and the same one the 6118 serve boots.
why: A press reached the wgpu node-graph surface for the first time in `📓️wgpu-node-graph-surface-retention-2026-09-13.md`, and reaching it showed that NONE of selecting a node, dragging a node, drawing a wire or cutting one was proven — and that a dense hover sweep killed the session outright. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, lane `wgpu-node-graph-gestures`.

rules.anUnchangedMoveCostsNothing: A pointer move that changes neither the selection, nor the hover target, nor the camera publishes NO action and reserves NO action credit. Pricing a plain hover like a mutation filled the 256-slot bounded action queue mid-sweep (`BoundedActionFault::ItemCredits`), after which the session published nothing at all for the rest of its life.
rules.aChangedMovePublishesOnlyWhatChanged: A move that changes one of the three publishes exactly that one. The change witness is the dispatched payload's own bytes, never a hand-maintained shadow of the fields that feed it.
rules.aDenseSweepSurvivesAnUndrainedQueue: Sweeping the whole surface on ONE never-drained `InputState` must not fault: the queue holds `ACTION_QUEUE_ITEM_CAPACITY` items and a sweep visits far more points than that.
rules.aBodyPressSelectsThatNode: A press on a node's draggable body — its rect minus its inline widgets and connector dots — replaces the graph selection with that one node. `DagScreenHit::is_draggable_body` is the ONE classification that says where that is, and the path discriminator reads the same one.
rules.aReleasedDragPublishesMove: A drag that ends somewhere else publishes `{operation: "move", nodeId, x, y}` per node it moved — once, on release, not once per pointer sample. Without it a bounded drag wrote the new positions into the fixture layout and told the guest nothing, so every dragged node snapped back on the next fixture push.
rules.aClickIsNotAMove: A press-and-release that ended where it started derives a zero-delta drag and must publish no `move` at all.
rules.aGestureBelongsToThePathThatStartedIt: While a BOUNDED gesture is in flight — a node drag, a marquee, a pan — a move must stay on the bounded path no matter what it passes over. Handing it to the screen path mid-flight resynced the interaction projection to IDLE, so the drag's own release saw no gesture to close: no `move` was journalled and the undo baseline it had armed stayed armed, which the next gesture then dropped unretired.
rules.aPortDragPublishesConnect: An output→input drag across two different nodes publishes `{operation: "connect", sourceNodeId, sourcePortId, targetNodeId, targetPortId}`. The board refuses output→output, input→input, same-node and cycle-forming pairs by design, so a failed pair proves nothing about the mechanism.
rules.aDetachedWirePublishesDisconnect: Dragging a WIRED input's endpoint off its port and releasing over empty canvas cuts the wire and publishes `{operation: "disconnect", synapseId}` naming the synapse the guest knows, never the engine's private edge number.
rules.aMinimapClickMovesTheCamera: A press inside the minimap panel but outside its viewport rectangle re-centres the camera and publishes the moved `nodeGraphViewport`.

graph.portDirections: A widget's `inputPorts[]` are its inputs; a synapse `{from, fromPort}` names an output and `{to, toPort}` an input. The fixture declares no `outputPorts` because outputs come from the neuron-kind catalogue, so the synapses are the only document-level witness of an output's id.
graph.neuronOutputsNeedTheCatalogue: A `neuron` widget's OUTPUT ports come from the app's registered operator catalogue, which rides the reserved `framework.section.catalogue` surface and is NOT part of `NodeGraphScene`. A scene carrying only `fixture_json` therefore materialises the three SLIDER outputs and none of the neuron ones, so `profile@wire`, `extrusion-axis@vectorOut` and `extrude@solid` — and the three synapses that use them — do not exist in this law's graph. Every case below is chosen to stand on the handles a catalogue-less scene really has; the 6118 serve, which does deliver the catalogue, hovers all six.
